::: {#fig-lp-space-singularity}

::: {.panel-tabset group="language"}

### R

```{r}
#| label: lp-space-singularity-r
#| fig-alt: >-
#|   Two side-by-side plots over x from 0 to 1, with the vertical axis cut off
#|   at 10. The left plot, titled p equals 1, shows the curve one over the
#|   square root of x falling steeply from 10 at x of 0.01 to 1 at x of
#|   1, with the area under it shaded blue; the area is 2. The right plot,
#|   titled p equals 2, shows the curve one over x, which rises past 10 at x of 0.1 and
#|   keeps climbing toward x of 0, with the area under it shaded vermilion and running off
#|   the top of the plot, because its area is infinite.
#| fig-height: 3.5
#| fig-width: 7
lpss_x_pf <- seq(0.01, 1, length.out = 400)
lpss_root_pf <- lpss_x_pf^(-1 / 2)
lpss_p1_pf <- tibble::tibble(
  x = lpss_x_pf, y = lpss_root_pf, panel = "p = 1: area = 2"
)
lpss_inv_pf <- 1 / lpss_x_pf
lpss_p2_pf <- tibble::tibble(
  x = lpss_x_pf, y = lpss_inv_pf, panel = "p = 2: area = infinity"
)
lpss_curves_pf <- dplyr::bind_rows(lpss_p1_pf, lpss_p2_pf)
lpss_aes_pf <- ggplot2::aes(x, y, fill = panel, colour = panel)
lpss_colours_pf <- c("#0072B2", "#D55E00")
ggplot2::ggplot(lpss_curves_pf, lpss_aes_pf) +
  ggplot2::geom_area(alpha = 0.3, colour = NA) +
  ggplot2::geom_line() +
  ggplot2::facet_wrap(ggplot2::vars(panel)) +
  ggplot2::scale_fill_manual(values = lpss_colours_pf) +
  ggplot2::scale_colour_manual(values = lpss_colours_pf) +
  ggplot2::coord_cartesian(ylim = c(0, 10)) +
  ggplot2::guides(fill = "none", colour = "none") +
  ggplot2::labs(x = "x", y = "|f(x)|^p")
```

### Python

```{python}
#| label: lp-space-singularity-python
#| fig-alt: >-
#|   Two side-by-side plots over x from 0 to 1, with the vertical axis cut off
#|   at 10. The left plot, titled p equals 1, shows the curve one over the
#|   square root of x falling steeply from 10 at x of 0.01 to 1 at x of
#|   1, with the area under it shaded blue; the area is 2. The right plot,
#|   titled p equals 2, shows the curve one over x, which rises past 10 at x of 0.1 and
#|   keeps climbing toward x of 0, with the area under it shaded vermilion and running off
#|   the top of the plot, because its area is infinite.
#| fig-height: 3.5
#| fig-width: 7
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import numpy as np

lpss_x_pf = np.linspace(0.01, 1, 400)
lpss_curves_pf = [
    ("p = 1: area = 2", lpss_x_pf ** (-1 / 2), "#0072B2"),
    ("p = 2: area = infinity", 1 / lpss_x_pf, "#D55E00"),
]
fig, axes = plt.subplots(1, 2, figsize=(7, 3.5), sharey=True,
                         layout="constrained")
for ax, (title, y, colour) in zip(axes, lpss_curves_pf):
    ax.fill_between(lpss_x_pf, y, color=colour, alpha=0.3)
    ax.plot(lpss_x_pf, y, color=colour)
    ax.set_title(title)
    ax.set_xlabel("x")
    ax.set_ylim(0, 10)
axes[0].set_ylabel("|f(x)|^p")
plt.show()
```

:::

The area under $\abs{f}^p$ for $f(x) = x^{-1/2}$ on $(0, 1)$ in @exm-lp-space.
The curve for $p = 1$ has area $2$, so $f \in \mathcal{L}^1$.
The curve for $p = 2$ keeps climbing toward $x = 0$ and its area is $\infty$,
so $f \notin \mathcal{L}^2$.
The plots cut the curves off at $10$.

:::
